title: Fed decision in April?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

March 2026 CPI accelerated to 3.3% year-over-year—the highest since May 2024—while nonfarm payrolls added 178,000 jobs against expectations of 60,000, with unemployment dipping to 4.3%, underscoring persistent inflation pressures and labor market strength that preclude cuts or hikes. March FOMC minutes, released April 8, signaled policy vigilance without urgency for adjustment, aligning with steady Treasury yields around 4.2%. Realistic challenges include a dovish dot plot shift or surprise Powell comments in today's announcement, though negligible alternative odds reflect baseline stability through mid-2026.

title: US x Iran ceasefire extended by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran announced on April 7, 2026, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed extension to the halt in direct military engagement between the United States and Iran, by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Both extensions of the April 7 ceasefire and new agreements scheduled to take effect before or at the initial agreement's scheduled end will be considered extensions of the ceasefire agreement, provided there is no period during which no ceasefire is in effect.

If a qualifying agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire extension ultimately takes effect. 

An extension of the ceasefire agreement requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another for longer than the initially agreed two-week period, or for an official extension of the ceasefire agreement in place to be otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation, or unilateral pause in hostilities without a confirmed agreement on a qualifying extension will not qualify. Similarly, newly agreed-upon humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not qualify.

A newly agreed-upon broader peace deal will qualify if it includes a qualifying extension of the ceasefire agreement/halt in military hostilities. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures, but do not explicitly commit to extending the ceasefire, will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire extension agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump unilaterally extended the initial two-week US-Iran ceasefire—agreed April 8 via Pakistani mediation—indefinitely on April 21, pending Tehran's submission of a permanent peace proposal, while upholding the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Iranian ports. Iran rejected the extension as meaningless, seized commercial vessels in retaliation, and shunned scheduled Islamabad talks, insisting on full blockade lift for any Strait reopening. Yesterday, Trump claimed Iranian officials privately admitted a "state of collapse," signaling potential negotiation leverage. With no fixed deadline and mutual provocations ongoing, traders weigh diplomatic breakthroughs against escalation risks from proxy actions or military posturing.

eventMetadata.context_description: The New York Knicks hold a 3-2 series lead over the Atlanta Hawks after Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns combined for dominant Game 5 performances at Madison Square Garden, fueling their momentum in this Eastern Conference first-round matchup. Hawks coach Quin Snyder countered with targeted defensive switches—Dyson Daniels on Towns, Nickeil Alexander-Walker on Brunson, and Onyeka Okongwu on OG Anunoby—but faltered late, highlighting frontcourt depth issues without injured center Jock Landale (right ankle). Game 6 shifts to State Farm Arena, where Atlanta's home-court advantage and desperation to force a Game 7 could exploit Knicks' road splits and minor fatigue from Brunson's recent ankle tweak, keeping the outcome closely contested amid resilient head-to-head trends.

eventMetadata.context_description: US intelligence agencies are evaluating potential Iranian retaliation if President Trump declares victory and halts military operations against Iran, per April 28 Reuters reporting, as the War Powers Resolution 60-day clock nears expiration on May 1 without congressional authorization. Operation Epic Fury, launched post joint US-Israel strikes on February 28 to dismantle Iranian capabilities, secured a ceasefire April 8—extended indefinitely April 21 pending Tehran's Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal—amid depleted US munitions and domestic pressure. The House rejected operational limits April 16, but Democrats signal post-deadline lawsuits. No formal end announcement has materialized despite Trump's hints of nearing completion, leaving traders focused on this week's diplomatic and legal catalysts.

title: Israel x Hezbollah Ceasefire extended by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official extension of the 10-day ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah announced on April 16, 2026, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed extension to the halt in direct military engagement between Israel and Hezbollah, by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Both extensions of the April 16 ceasefire and new agreements scheduled to take effect before or at the initial agreement's scheduled end will be considered extensions of the ceasefire agreement, provided there is no period during which no ceasefire is in effect.

If a qualifying agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire extension ultimately takes effect.

An extension of the ceasefire agreement requires clear public confirmation from both the Israeli government and Hezbollah that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another for longer than the initially agreed 10-day period, or for an official extension of the ceasefire agreement in place to be otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation, or unilateral pause in hostilities without a confirmed agreement on a qualifying extension will not qualify. Similarly, newly agreed-upon humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not qualify.

A newly agreed-upon broader peace deal will qualify if it includes a qualifying extension of the ceasefire agreement/halt in military hostilities. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures, but do not explicitly commit to extending the ceasefire, will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the Israeli government and Hezbollah. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire extension agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: A US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, initially set for 10 days starting April 16, was extended by three weeks on April 24 following White House talks between Israeli and Lebanese envoys, as announced by President Trump. However, the truce remains fragile amid mutual accusations of violations: Israel reports over 15 Hezbollah drone and rocket incursions in recent days, prompting IDF airstrikes on terrorist infrastructure south of the Litani River, while Hezbollah cites ongoing Israeli operations and evacuation orders as breaches. Diplomatic pressures from the US aim to enable broader peace negotiations, but escalating tit-for-tat strikes risk collapse before the May mid-point expiry, with traders eyeing compliance signals and potential UN mediation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom holds a commanding 27% implied probability as trader consensus frontrunner for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination in a wide-open field following the party's 2024 defeat, bolstered by a March 2026 California poll showing him leading Kamala Harris by 14 points in their home state and his sustained national profile as a Trump critic with strong fundraising. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 8.6% draws progressive enthusiasm amid debates over her presidential or Senate ambitions, while Harris at 7.5% faces skepticism despite her April 10 signals of interest at the National Action Network convention, weighed by prior campaign baggage. Jon Ossoff's recent surge to 6.3% reflects Georgia incumbency appeal. Consolidation could hinge on 2026 midterm performances for governors like Newsom and senators, early-state polling, DNC rules, and superdelegate endorsements.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile two-week ceasefire agreed on April 8 following escalation in the 2026 Iran war—including U.S. enforcement of a Strait of Hormuz blockade—U.S.-Iran negotiations mediated by Pakistan continue in Islamabad, with Iran submitting a new three-phase proposal on April 27 to end hostilities and reopen the strait in exchange for sanctions relief and security guarantees. The White House is reviewing the offer amid persistent rifts over Iran's nuclear enrichment, ballistic missiles, and regional proxies, as highlighted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. While an interim truce extension appears likely before the ceasefire expires, a permanent peace deal faces steep hurdles including congressional oversight for any nuclear components and maximalist demands from both sides. Traders watch for the next mediation round and U.S. response, which could signal progress or renewed tensions.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the frontrunner at 49% implied probability for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, driven by his high-profile role as HHS Secretary and the growing Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement appealing to GOP base voters skeptical of establishment figures. Vice President J.D. Vance holds 38.6% amid incumbency advantages and strong showings in recent CPAC (53%) and Echelon Insights (42%) polls, though his odds dipped following foreign policy setbacks like failed Iran negotiations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's 21.9% reflects rising White House insider buzz from his diplomatic profile, including recent Iran war positioning debates, positioning the field as closely contested ahead of 2026 midterms.

title: Will the Iranian regime fall by May 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus heavily favors no Iranian regime fall by May 31, reflecting the leadership's sustained control through intensified crackdowns, including execution sprees and mass arrests reported in early April amid fears of uprisings. Protests, sparked by economic crisis since late 2025 and escalated by US-Israel airstrikes and the reported assassination of Supreme Leader Khamenei, have been suppressed via internet shutdowns and security force loyalty from the IRGC, preventing widespread defections or opposition seizures of key institutions. With the war showing de-escalation signals like Trump's claims of nearing completion, no unified rebel advances have materialized. Realistic shifts could arise from IRGC mutinies, a successful opposition coalition, or intensified external military actions fracturing command structures.

title: Who will be confirmed as Fed Chair?
description:
This market will resolve according to the next individual formally confirmed as Chair of the Federal Reserve.

Formal confirmation as Chair of the Federal Reserve requires the Senate to confirm a nominee as Chair of the Federal Reserve. Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count. Senate confirmation of a listed individual as a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors will not alone qualify.

If no Senate confirmation for the position of Chair of the Federal Reserve has occurred by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from the U.S. Senate; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's March nomination of former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed Chair—whose term expires May 15—has solidified trader consensus at 98.8%, driven by Warsh's April 21 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing where he pledged Fed independence amid grilling on potential White House influence. Recent momentum includes Senator Tillis signaling readiness to lift his hold tied to the Powell investigation, with a committee vote planned imminently amid Republican Senate control favoring swift confirmation. Challenges could arise from unexpected bipartisan opposition, procedural delays like filibusters, nominee withdrawal, or late scandals, though historical patterns for aligned nominees suggest low risk before Powell's planned holdover as acting chair.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the listed driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2026 F1 season.

This market will resolve as soon as the official results of the final scheduled race of the 2026 F1 season are known.

If multiple drivers tie for first place in the drivers standings, this market will resolve according to the tiebreak procedure used by F1 to determine the 2026 F1 Drivers’ champion.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2026 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes teammates George Russell and Kimi Antonelli dominate the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship after three Grands Prix, with the 19-year-old rookie Antonelli leading at 72 points ahead of Russell's 63, thanks to back-to-back wins in China and Japan following Russell's Australian GP opener victory. Trader consensus prices Russell at 41.5% implied probability to claim the title—edging Antonelli's 32.6%—reflecting his experience and consistency in the intra-team battle amid Mercedes' superior new power unit performance, while youth volatility tempers bets on the leader. Charles Leclerc sits third at 49 points (7.0%), with McLaren's Oscar Piastri (5.3%) and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton (3.5%) trailing; Red Bull's Max Verstappen lags at 3.3% after early struggles. No major incidents post-Japan GP, but Miami's upcoming street circuit could test tire strategy and qualifying pace.

title: What will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit in April 2026?
description: What will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit in April 2026?

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $160 in April?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point during April 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For WTI futures, the active month refers to the nearest listed contract month. The active month changes at 6:00:00 PM ET at the start of the trading session two business days prior to that contract's last trading day, at which point the next listed contract becomes the active month.

For WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, the last trading day is defined as three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day), consistent with CME contract specifications.

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours as listed on Pyth.

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles.

Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point during April 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For WTI futures, the active month refers to the nearest listed contract month. The active month changes at 6:00:00 PM ET at the start of the trading session two business days prior to that contract's last trading day, at which point the next listed contract becomes the active month.

For WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, the last trading day is defined as three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day), consistent with CME contract specifications.

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours as listed on Pyth.

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles.

Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil futures have rallied above $100 per barrel as of April 29, 2026, propelled by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and stalled peace talks keeping the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, tightening global supply amid persistent demand from Asia. OPEC+ decisions to gradually unwind cuts—adding 206,000 barrels per day starting April—have provided limited offset, while U.S. EIA inventories showed a 1.925 million barrel build for the week ending April 17, tempering bullish momentum. Trader consensus reflects skin-in-the-game bets on sustained supply risks outweighing softening manufacturing signals. Key catalysts ahead include weekly EIA storage reports and potential OPEC+ adjustments in May, with resolution hinging on end-month settlement levels amid volatility.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

If at any point it is impossible for the listed candidate to win Eurovision 2026 based on the rules of the competition (i.e. they are eliminated), this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen lead trader consensus at 35.3% implied probability to win Eurovision 2026 in Vienna, propelled by their UMK national final victory in late February with the violin-driven pop anthem "Liekinheitin," which dominates fan polls, OGAE votes, and bookmaker odds through strong jury and televote appeal. Denmark's Søren Torpegaard Lund has surged to 13.4% following robust pre-party buzz for "Før vi går hjem," overtaking Greece's Akylas ("Ferto," 11.5%), whose "Super Ferto" remix dropped last week to boost streaming traction. France's pre-qualified Monroe ("Regarde!") holds steady at 10.2% amid Big Five momentum. With all 35 entries released and first rehearsals underway, live staging and semi-final qualifiers on May 12-14 will be pivotal swing factors before the May 16 grand final.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by end of April?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and April 30, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for April 30, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance leads narrowly over California Governor Gavin Newsom in trader consensus for the 2028 presidential election, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio third, as prediction markets price in Vance's incumbency edge from the Trump administration and Newsom's prominence as a leading Democratic critic. A late-March UMass Lowell poll showed Vance ahead 33%-30% in a hypothetical matchup, supporting his position despite recent foreign policy challenges like Iran negotiations. The field stays tightly contested given the two-year horizon to November 2028, uncertainty over 2026 midterm outcomes, and Trump's potential endorsement influence. Separation could arise from strong midterm performances, key primary endorsements, sustained polling leads, or shifts in economic conditions and party dynamics.

title: LoL: Fnatic vs Shifters (BO3) - Esports World Cup EMEA Qualifier Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Upper bracket round 1 match between Fnatic and Shifters in the Esports World Cup EMEA Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for April 28 at 11:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Fnatic" if Fnatic win the match against Shifters.

This market will resolve to "Shifters" if Shifters win the match against Fnatic.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Fnatic entered the Esports World Cup 2026 EMEA Qualifier BO3 matchup as clear trader favorites, buoyed by a dominant 2-0 sweep over Shifters in LEC Spring Week 5 Day 1 just four days earlier, where Razork and Vladi outclassed nuc and Boukada in macro and skirmishes. Shifters slumped at 0-7 in LEC regular season standings with an 18% game win rate, extending a seven-series losing streak, while mid-table Fnatic (2-5, 7th place) showed playoff viability. Both field stable 2026 rosters—Fnatic's Empyros, Razork, Vladi, Upset, Lospa versus Shifters' Rooster/Boukada, nuc, Paduck, Trymbi—amid a patch favoring aggressive jungle paths suiting Fnatic's style. Double-elimination format adds upset potential, with winner advancing to face G2 Esports.

title: Trump announces US blockade of Hormuz lifted by...?
description:
On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump directed aides to prepare for an extended US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on April 28, underscoring a strategy of sustained economic pressure on Iran after recent peace talks collapsed in Islamabad and earlier direct negotiations failed around April 12. The blockade, enforced by US Central Command to restrict ships accessing Iranian ports, followed Iran's reported mine-laying and counter-closure threats, prompting US mine-clearing operations. Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the strait contingent on lifted US sanctions remains unaccepted, with no lifting announcement issued amid shifting diplomacy involving Russia as a potential mediator. Traders weigh these stalled bilateral dynamics, oil market volatility, and escalation risks against prospects for de-escalation before May deadlines.

title: LoL: Weibo Gaming vs Top Esports (BO3) - LPL Group Ascend
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between Weibo Gaming and Top Esports in the LPL Group Ascend, initially scheduled for April 28 at 7:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Weibo Gaming" if Weibo Gaming win the match against Top Esports.

This market will resolve to "Top Esports" if Top Esports win the match against Weibo Gaming.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Top Esports entered as Group Ascend frontrunners with a 6-1 series record and +10 game differential, riding a dominant win streak that included 2-0 sweeps over Bilibili Gaming, JD Gaming, and Ninjas in Pyjamas, fueled by Tian's aggressive jungle paths, Creme's mid-lane stability, and JackeyLove's bot-lane dominance. Weibo Gaming languished at 2-6, rebounding from 0-2 losses to BLG and 1-2 to Anyone's Legend with a 2-0 over Team WE, relying on Jiejie's ganks, Xiaohu's macro, and Elk's scaling threats amid support Hang's recent integration. Historical head-to-head favors TES 11-5 overall, though WBG upset them in Split 1 playoffs; BO3 format and current patch's objective focus amplify TES' macro edge in double round-robin play.

title: Elon Musk # tweets April 24 - May 1, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from April 24 12:00 PM ET to May 1, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding US-Iranian relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count. 

The meeting must be in-person and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: US-Iran diplomatic efforts remain stalled following indirect negotiations mediated by Pakistan in Islamabad earlier this month, where anticipated face-to-face talks involving US Vice President JD Vance and Iranian officials like Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi failed to materialize. Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid its blockade is under White House review, but Tehran announced no date for the next round on April 18, with its top diplomat blaming Washington for impasse during a recent Russia visit. Fresh US sanctions on Iranian entities announced April 29 underscore hardening positions, while traders monitor potential ceasefire extensions and nuclear talks for any de-escalation signals before key deadlines.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices a low likelihood of Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic returning to normal by May 15 amid the ongoing 2026 US-Iran crisis, where mutual blockades persist following failed ceasefire negotiations. US Central Command's blockade of Iranian ports, implemented in mid-April, prompted Iranian Revolutionary Guard attacks and seizures of three vessels last week, reducing transits to under 10% of pre-crisis levels—recently as few as five ships daily versus the normal 140. Iran's Deputy Parliamentary Speaker explicitly rejected a return to prior free shipping norms while the US blockade remains, with shipping data showing sparse, mostly Iran-linked passages and no surge in oil or gas flows despite minor upticks to 19 vessels on April 27. Experts forecast weeks or months for phased recovery, barring diplomatic breakthroughs.

title: LoL: FlyQuest vs Team Liquid (BO3) - Esports World Cup North America Qualifier Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Lower bracket final match between FlyQuest and Team Liquid in the Esports World Cup North America Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for April 28 at 2:00PM ET.

This market will resolve to "FlyQuest" if FlyQuest win the match against Team Liquid.

This market will resolve to "Team Liquid" if Team Liquid win the match against FlyQuest.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

markets.question: First Blood in Game 1?
markets.description:
In the upcoming Lower bracket final match between FlyQuest and Team Liquid in the Esports World Cup North America Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for April 28 at 2:00PM ET:

This market will resolve to the team that secures the first blood in Game 1.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If Game 1 begins but is not completed, this market will resolve to whichever team secured the first blood prior to stoppage. If the first blood did not occur, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is remade, this market will resolve to whichever team secured the first blood prior to the remake. If the first blood did not occur prior to the remake, resolution will be based on the remade game.

If Game 1 is completed but first blood never occurred, this market will resolve to 50-50.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

eventMetadata.context_description: FlyQuest and Team Liquid clash in the lower bracket final of the Esports World Cup 2026 North America Qualifier playoffs, a pivotal BO3 where the winner advances to a Bo5 grand final against Sentinels for the sole NA slot at the main event. Team Liquid rides high atop LCS 2026 Spring Split standings at 4-0, powered by veteran imports Morgan (top), Josedeodo (jungle), Quid (mid), Yeon (ADC), and CoreJJ (support), emphasizing dominant macro and objective control. FlyQuest sits 2-2 in LCS but stunned TL 2-1 earlier in this double-elim bracket on April 14, leveraging Gryffinn's jungle paths, Quad's midlaning, and late-game scaling from Gakgos and Cryogen amid Patch 26.8's teamfight meta. Head-to-head history tilts TL overall (20-13), yet FLY's qualifier momentum heightens upset risk in this high-pressure elimination match.
